author: GamingBolt
description:
Onimusha: Way of the Sword has been a long time coming. The samurai horror series has been dormant for nearly two decades, but the franchise is back with a new protagonist, a new setting, and numerous noteworthy updates to how its signature swordplay works. The original magic is still present though, with Way of the Sword revolving around Genma, new powers, and Issen. 

The key difference, however, is that these familiarities have been rebuilt around a modern action-game framework. Yet, if you’ve played Onimusha: Warlords, Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny, Onimusha 3: Demon Siege, and Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams, you’ll know that there are plenty more changes between the original four and Way of the Sword.
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword vs. The Original PS2 Games - 15 BIGGEST Differences

author: GamingBolt
description:
On first glance, Control Resonant looks like Remedy abandoning what made Control distinctive. Yes, both games share the same anomalous weirdness, but Jesse Faden’s foundational descent into the bowels of The Oldest House was much less a character-focused journey than Resonant appears. 

The setting itself, the amorphous concrete of the FBC’s headquarters, was the story. Now, Remedy is extrapolating that strangeness to a different location, and they’re asking you to go and find the hidden stories for yourself through the eyes of Jesse’s brother.
title: Why Control Resonant Is Looking Like Remedy's Best Game Yet
